What a symbolized GLLVM should explain

Source: vignettes/symbolizer-gllvm-design.Rmd
symbolizer-gllvm-design.Rmd

1. Why a design target

A generalised linear latent variable model (GLLVM) is more than its likelihood. It is a story about shared between-trait variation, trait- specific noise, latent axes, and identifiability constraints. A symbolizer surface for any GLLVM has to explain all four. This page is the contract. It says what a complete answer looks like when symbolize.gllvmTMB() returns its symbolized_model, and it pins each item of the contract to the field of the object where you would find that answer.

The companion vignette symbolizer-gllvm is the worked example: one fit, one set of accessors, one biological reading. This vignette is the target the worked example is aimed at. Every promise made here either lands as a populated row of symbolized_model in the v0.4 First slice, or is flagged “v0.5” or “planned” when it is on the roadmap but not yet in.

Takeaway. This page is the contract — what symbolize.gllvmTMB() must surface, and where in the returned symbolized_model a reader should look for each piece.

2. The structural equation, both notations

The GLLVM has the same shape in two notations. Index form (one equation per observation, per Eq. 11 of the Nakagawa et al. trait- covariance framework):

yijt=μt+∑k=1dBλtkzik+sit+eijt y_{ijt} = \mu_t + \sum_{k=1}^{d_B} \lambda_{tk}\, z_{ik} + s_{it} + e_{ijt}

Index ii ranges over the between-unit replicate (individual, site, or species), jj over the row, tt over the trait, kk over the latent axis. The four pieces are: μt\mu_t the trait grand mean; ∑kλtkzik\sum_k \lambda_{tk} z_{ik} the shared low-rank between-unit signal; sits_{it} the trait-specific between-unit deviation; eijte_{ijt} the within-unit (across-row) residual.

Matrix form (one block for the whole dataset):

𝐘=𝟏𝛍⊤+𝐙𝚲⊤+𝐒+𝐄 \mathbf{Y} = \mathbf{1}\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\!\top} + \mathbf{Z}\,\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^{\!\top} + \mathbf{S} + \mathbf{E}

𝐘\mathbf{Y} is the n×Tn \times T matrix of trait values, 𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu} the length-TT vector of trait means, 𝐙\mathbf{Z} the n×dBn \times d_B matrix of latent scores, 𝚲\boldsymbol{\Lambda} the T×dBT \times d_B loading matrix, 𝐒\mathbf{S} the n×Tn \times T matrix of trait-specific between-unit deviations (rows distributed as 𝒩(𝟎,𝚿B)\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Psi}_B) with 𝚿B=diag(ψB,1,…,ψB,T)\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B = \mathrm{diag}(\psi_{B,1}, \ldots, \psi_{B,T})), and 𝐄\mathbf{E} the within-unit residual.

A symbolizer surface must carry both forms. Index form is the one a reader instantiates row by row; matrix form is the one a reader uses to see the linear algebra of the fit.

Takeaway. Both notations live in equations(sym) and on the equation / equation_matrix columns of components(sym).

3. The decomposition that matters most: 𝚺B=𝚲B𝚲B⊤+𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B^\top + \boldsymbol{\Psi}_B

The between-unit trait covariance is the deliverable of a GLLVM in ecology and evolution. It decomposes additively: the shared low-rank piece 𝚲B𝚲B⊤\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B^\top holds the covariation that travels through the latent axes; the diagonal 𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B holds the trait-specific between-unit variance that is not captured by the axes.

Symbol Meaning gllvmTMB accessor Biological reading
𝚺B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B Implied between-unit trait covariance extract_Omega(fit) Total between-unit trait covariance the model implies.
𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B Shared low-rank loadings (trait by axis) getLoadings(fit) How strongly trait tt loads on latent axis kk.
𝚲B𝚲B⊤\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B^\top Shared communality (rank-dBd_B covariance from the axes) extract_communality(fit) Variance shared across traits through the latent axes.
𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B Trait-specific unique between-unit variance getResidualCov(fit)$Psi Variance left after the shared axes; trait-specific noise.
𝐂B=𝐃B−1/2𝚺B𝐃B−1/2\mathbf{C}_B = \mathbf{D}_B^{-1/2} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B \mathbf{D}_B^{-1/2} Between-unit trait correlation extract_correlations(fit) Positive entries are behavioural syndromes; negative entries are antagonistic axes.

The five rows are not five independent quantities — they are five views of the same between-unit trait covariance, each one tuned to a different audience. A reader who wants the headline number wants 𝐂B\mathbf{C}_B; a reader who wants the mechanism wants 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B; a reader who wants to know how much was not explained wants 𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B.

Takeaway. A symbolized GLLVM must carry all five rows. The 𝚲B𝚲B⊤+𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B^\top + \boldsymbol{\Psi}_B identity is the bridge; the other three rows are derived views.

4. What symbolize() must populate

The symbol table below lists the symbolized_model fields a fitted GLLVM should populate and the accessor that reads each field.

Field What it carries Accessor
model Fitted-object class, family, response, and model dimensions (nn, TT, dBd_B). sym$model
submodels One row per coefficient family: 𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu} (trait intercepts) and 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B (between-unit loadings). sym$submodels
terms Per-trait intercept rows from the 0 + trait design, each tagged role = "trait_intercept". sym$terms
loadings One row per (λB,tk\lambda_{B,tk}) loading entry with estimate and SE. sym$loadings
variance_components Diagonal of 𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B (per-trait unique SD) and the shared row residual σϵ\sigma_\epsilon. sym$variance_components
components Distribution, linear predictor, latent score distribution 𝐳B,i∼𝒩(𝟎,𝐈dB)\mathbf{z}_{B,i} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I}_{d_B}), and the implied covariance row 𝚺B=𝚲B𝚲B⊤+𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B^\top + \boldsymbol{\Psi}_B. components(sym)
assumptions Conditional independence given 𝐳B,i\mathbf{z}_{B,i}, standard-Gaussian latent prior, lower-triangular rotation convention, missing trait cells, biological reading of 𝚺B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B. assumption_table(sym)
symbol_dictionary 𝐘\mathbf{Y}, 𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu}, 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B, 𝐙B\mathbf{Z}_B, 𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B, σϵ\sigma_\epsilon, 𝚺B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B — each with abstract and concrete dimensions. symbol_table(sym)
formula_bridge R syntax (0 + trait, latent(0 + trait &#124; unit, d = K)) mapped to the corresponding math in both notations. formula_bridge(sym)
interpretation Per-trait intercept and per-loading prose, on link / natural / variance / biological scales. parameter_interpretation(sym)

Two fields deserve a closer look. components is where the four structural lines of section 2 live, one row each: the distribution, the linear predictor for 𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu}, the latent score distribution, and the implied-covariance row. assumptions is where the rotation and sign ambiguity (section 6 below) and the standard-Gaussian latent prior are stated explicitly so a reader knows what the loading matrix does and does not pin down.

Takeaway. Ten populated fields. The contract is that a symbolized_ model from a Gaussian GLLVM First slice carries all ten of them; a renderer never has to read the fit again.

5. The hard truth of capabilities

Not every GLLVM is in scope yet. The capability registry (symbolizer_capabilities()) gates symbolize() against the family, class, and component tuple of the incoming fit. The gllvmTMB rows look like this:

class family component status
gllvmTMB gaussian mu First slice
gllvmTMB gaussian Lambda_B First slice
gllvmTMB gaussian Sigma_B First slice
gllvmTMB gaussian Psi_B First slice
gllvmTMB gaussian sigma_eps First slice
gllvmTMB * Lambda_W Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB * Psi_W Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB * phylo Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB * spatial Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB * Sigma Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB binomial * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB poisson * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB nbinom2 * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB Gamma * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB lognormal * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB Beta * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB betabinomial * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB tweedie * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB student * Planned or reserved
gllvmTMB ordinal_probit * Planned or reserved

The five gllvmTMB Gaussian rows — 𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu}, 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B, 𝚺B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B, 𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B, σϵ\sigma_\epsilon — are First slice in v0.4. Everything else is planned. In particular, the within-unit decomposition (𝚲W\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_W, 𝚿W\boldsymbol{\Psi}_W) is planned for v0.5. Non-Gaussian families (Bernoulli, Poisson, negative binomial, beta, gamma, tweedie, ordinal) are planned for later v0.5 / v0.6 work. Phylogenetic and spatial covstructs are planned beyond that.

symbolize() will refuse to read a fit whose family or structure is not in the registry as Stable or First slice. The error message lists the currently-readable tuples so the user sees what they can do today. This is intentional: a symbolic surface that silently dropped unsupported terms would be more dangerous than no surface at all.

Takeaway. Gaussian, between-unit, reduced-rank-plus-diagonal is in. Everything else is planned and is rejected by the registry until its row turns First slice.

6. Identifiability gotchas a biologist must know

The loading matrix 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B is identified only up to rotation and sign when dB>1d_B > 1. Two fits that produce indistinguishable likelihoods can have entirely different-looking 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B. This is the classical factor-analysis identifiability problem. The implied between-unit covariance 𝚺B=𝚲B𝚲B⊤+𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B^\top + \boldsymbol{\Psi}_B is invariant under rotation; 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B itself is not.

A symbolizer surface has to be explicit about this. There are two practical conventions, both surfaced in assumption_table(sym):

  • Lower-triangular 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B for confirmatory use — pin the upper triangle to zero so each column has a designated leading trait. This is the default identification gllvmTMB uses on fitting. It produces a unique solution but its columns are not maximally interpretable.
  • Varimax-rotated 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B for interpretation — rotate the fitted loadings so each axis loads strongly on a small set of traits and near zero on the rest. The rotation is applied after fitting and preserves 𝚺B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B. The column labels may reorder under rotation; the block structure is what the reader interprets.

symbolize.gllvmTMB() returns the as-fit (lower-triangular) 𝚲B\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B in sym$loadings. The assumption rows for the fit carry a sentence each on the rotation and sign conventions so a reader does not mistake non-uniqueness for non-replicability. The worked-example vignette (symbolizer-gllvm) shows the varimax-rotated matrix on the reader-facing side.

Takeaway. Rotation and sign ambiguity are stated assumptions, not bugs. The implied covariance is invariant; the loadings are not.

7. What comes next (v0.5+)

Three extensions are on the roadmap but not in the v0.4 First slice:

  • Within-unit decomposition. v0.5 will surface 𝚲W\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_W and 𝚿W\boldsymbol{\Psi}_W — the reduced-rank-plus-diagonal decomposition of the within-unit trait covariance — so a fit with two latent(...) terms (one for between-unit, one for within-unit) carries the same Σ-bridge table twice, once per tier.
  • Phylogenetic and spatial structured latents. Planned for the release after v0.5: phylo_rr, phylo_diag, spde, and spatial covstructs. The structural surface gains a phylogenetic / spatial covariance row alongside 𝚺B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B.
  • Non-Gaussian families. Bernoulli (joint species distribution models from presence-absence), Poisson (count communities), negative binomial, beta, gamma, tweedie, ordinal probit are planned. The Σ-bridge generalises: the response covariance is read on the link scale via 𝚺B=𝚲B𝚲B⊤+𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_B = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B^\top + \boldsymbol{\Psi}_B, but 𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B’s interpretation changes — for example, in the Bernoulli case the diagonal residual variance is fixed by the link, so 𝚿B\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B is the extra over-dispersion above what the link supplies.

Takeaway. v0.4 covers Gaussian, between-unit, reduced-rank-plus- diagonal. The Σ-bridge generalises one tier at a time as the registry turns each planned row into a First slice.
